title: Horizon routing policy: latency-windowed affinity with capacity credits and graceful shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We currently use simple latency-first routing + geo pinning with static thresholds. During regional congestion or partial outages we see two failure modes: 1) excessive cross-region hedging causing capacity pressure in adjacent regions, and 2) brittle circuit trips that cause sudden mass failovers and client-perceived latency spikes.

Goal: Design and implement a new routing policy (Horizon Routing) that: (a) uses short latency windows to make routing decisions that minimize unnecessary cross-region traffic, (b) attaches capacity credits to region pins to prevent single regions from being overdrawn, (c) supports multi-tier circuit breakers (soft warn, hardened degrade, full trip) and integrates soft load-shedding to preserve SLOs, and (d) exposes conservative knobs for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Scope: prototype policy and simulation, runtime integration (request director), control plane knobs in Console, dashboards and SLO change events, canary rollout plan, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation: synthetic traffic with bursty latency shows Horizon reduces cross-region tail latency by >=15% vs baseline under constrained capacity scenarios
Safety: under sustained overload Horizon maintains region utilization <= 95% on-pool due to capacity credits and shedding
SLO impact: 99th percentile tail latency for customer-facing generation endpoints does not regress beyond a configurable guardrail (default 3%) during rollout
Observability: per-route time-series for latency-window decisions, credit balances, circuit tier, and shed rates are available in Console and Grafana
Rollout: policy is behind a runtime flag and can be toggled by customer tier and region; canary shows no customer-facing errors for 48h before wide rollout
decisions: Use a 30s rolling latency window (configurable per-route) as the primary measurement for affinity decisions to avoid reacting to single-sample spikes
Attach a credit bucket to each region-model pair (credits measured in effective tokens equal to QPS * credit_window_seconds) to throttle additional pinning when pool is near capacity
Circuit model: three tiers — WARN (log + minimal reroutes), SOFT-DEGRADE (probabilistic reroute and lightweight shedding), HARD-TRIP (stop pinning and route away until recovery)
Soft-shedding uses token-bucket per-customer with dynamic shed_fraction computed from credit deficit and SLO priority
Expose conservative defaults for Dedicated/Private orgs but allow tuned policies via Console policies and a new routing config schema
